utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-A, the Prosecutor versus Fatmir Limaj, Haradin Bala, and Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, registrar. I understand that both counsel for Mr. Musliu and counsel for Mr. Bala will be with us by teleconference. Because of technological limitations, we can only have one of them with us at a time. Accordingly, for the first few minutes I wish to deal exclusively with the appeals related to Mr. Limaj and to Mr. Musliu. Mr. Bala, we shall turn to you once your counsel is on the teleconference, so you can be seated now. THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Could I now, please, have the appearances of the parties in the appeals related to Mr. Limaj and Mr. Musliu. First the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Katharina Margetts, together with Shelagh McCall and our case manager, Mr. Sebastiaan van Hooydonk. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it please Your Honour, Karim Khan for Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Thank you, Ms. Margetts. Now, counsel for Mr. Musliu who should be with us by teleconference, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Good afternoon, Your Honour, yes, Steven Powles appearing by telephone link on behalf of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Powles. This is, as you know, a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I understand that Mr. Limaj and Mr. Musliu, who are not currently incarcerated, are not attending this Status Conference. Would their respective counsel kindly confirm that for the record, Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Your Honour, yes, that's correct on behalf of Mr. Musliu as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Powles, I would like to say a word to you, if I may. I note that the Scheduling Order of 7 June 2007 stated, and I quote: "Should counsel for a defendant seek to participate by teleconference rather than in person, counsel should file the written consent of his client to this effect at least one week prior to the Status Conference." You have, I'm sorry to say, not only failed to meet the deadline of one week notice, but you have failed to file any such written consent at all. I'm distressed by this lapse, and I would like to know whether I have your assurances that such a consent will be filed retroactively as soon as possible. Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Your Honour, yes. May I firstly of course offer my unreserved apologies for the tardiness in the filing of such a document, and secondly, give my assurance that such a document will be filed in due course as soon as it is able to make contact with Mr. Musliu and obtain his written consent accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: If such a filing, Mr. Powles, is swiftly made and is otherwise adequate, it shall be deemed valid without any further order from me, but I emphasise it must be filed swiftly.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] I am grateful for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Before asking any questions, I wish to note for everyone's benefit that the Appeals Chamber is working on the draft judgement, and my tentative guess is that we will issue it sometime not too long after the summer recess. Now I want to ask counsel for Mr. Limaj and for Mr. Musliu whether there are any issues that their clients would like to raise through counsel and also whether they have any other issues to raise at this time. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am grateful. There's no issues to be raised on behalf of Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Your Honour, no issues to specifically raise on behalf of Mr. Musliu, save to give my -- my thanks to all the registry and in particular to your legal assistant, Ms. Jean Galbraith, for very helpfully facilitating my possibility for appearing by telephone link today at such short notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like now to turn to the Prosecution and ask them whether they have any issues regarding the appeals related to Mr. Limaj or to Mr. Musliu that they would like to raise. The Prosecution, Ms. Margaret.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, there's nothing on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Margaret. Since this concludes all issues in relation to Mr. Musliu, we will say good-bye to Mr. Powles and wait for a moment while the technical team establishes contact with Mr. Guy-Smith. Good-bye, Mr. Powles. Mr. Powles? Mr. Powles must have decided that he's now functo officio with regard to this Status Conference and we will accept that -- I'm waiting for Mr. Guy-Smith to come on the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So we -- this is Judge Meron and welcome to the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Hello, Judge Meron, how are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Thank you for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, before turning to the substance of the Status Conference --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- I wish also to make sure that Mr. Bala who is present today can follow these proceedings. Mr. Bala, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? Mr. Bala? THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. You may be seated. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case held on 21 March 2007. As Mr. Bala is currently detained in the United Nations Detention Unit, I would like to start by asking Mr. Bala whether there are any issues that he would like to raise at this time. Mr. Bala, do you have any issues or concerns that you would like to raise, especially concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being? I understand that you recently you have undergone heart surgery, and I hope that you are recovering. Mr. Bala. THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. After the surgery, I can freely say that I feel much better, but my overall health is not that good because I'm facing some other health problems. For example, I have problems with my eyesight and with lungs, among others. Therefore, overall I would say that my health is not satisfactory; however, I undergo regular treatment and therapy. We'll see how these things develop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala. It is my hope that you will get better soon with regard to all of your health concerns, and I wish you well in that regard. You may now sit down, Mr. Bala. THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] By your leave, I would like to add something, Your Honour. As far as the appeals session is concerned, I would like to apologise to the Trial Chamber and all those present, during the second day of the appeals hearing for not being able to be present on that day, and this was because of health reasons. And I would like to thank the Appeals Chamber for allowing me not to be present on that day. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bala, for the comment you have just made. Of course I can assure you that the Appeals Chamber was well aware of the fact that you had to absent yourself for good reasons of health, which we fully accept. Anything else, Mr. Bala? THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] That would be all, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, and you may be seated. THE APPELLANT BALA: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now I would like to note for Mr. Guy-Smith's benefit that I mentioned -- that as I mentioned to the others earlier, the Appeals Chamber is working on the draft judgement, and my tentative guess is that we will issue it sometimes not too long after the summer recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, do you have any issues you would wish to raise at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Via teleconference] I have no issues that I wish to raise at this time, Your Honour, and I thank you very much for the information concerning when judgement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution have any issues to raise with regard to the appeals related to Mr. Bala?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, there's nothing on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Margetts. On that note, I thank the parties for their attendance today, and I also thank our technical team for making our teleconferencing possible. I call the proceedings to a close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.14 p.m.
